The banking system remains sound but faces risks from financial leverage and asset valuations. International growth was weak, with AFEs hit by monetary policy tightening and high inflation. Many central banks are expected to ease monetary policy in 2024.

The Federal Reserve has reduced its securities holdings while providing liquidity to banks. Employment and earnings have improved for disadvantaged groups, but disparities remain. Bank lending conditions have tightened due to monetary policy and banking sector strains.

The Federal Reserve monitors financial risks and implements policies to ensure a stable financial system supporting the U.S. economy.

The Federal Reserve assesses four key vulnerabilities (business borrowing, leverage, asset valuations, funding risk) for financial stability. Monitoring these helps inform broader policy discussions and research.
